canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Canonical review uses the single reviewer result from epic-reviewer-2.
crossStoryFindings: Stories 2, 4, 5, and 6 are mostly coherent: capture, turn derivation, fork replay, inference routing, and startup validation all run through connector entry points and real LHC surfaces.

Story 1 thread identity drift remains material: the current code both adds a PI custom-entry thread pointer and still keeps a cwd-most-recent fallback, while the epic and tech design describe launch/registry resolution with no PI-session-to-thread mapping.
Story 3 does not meet the epic-level verification contract because the corpus loaders are synthetic stand-ins rather than recorded PI corpora.
architectureFindings: Epic 1 correctly remains observe-only: index.ts registers no context hook and capture does not alter what PI serves to the model.
The converter architecture matches the tech design: map-message is pure, turn-accumulator owns the LHC turn boundary, and converter writes through intakeStream.messageEvents.

The current reload implementation conflicts with the tech design resolution of I-1/I-7: tech-design.md says there is no stored PI-session-to-thread pointer, but index.ts writes and reads a pi-lhc-thread-state custom entry via appendEntry/sessionManager.
The production --resume default does not resolve an operator selection. It notifies the candidate list, auto-resolves only one candidate, and returns null for multiple candidates.

Fork seeding uses the real intake path and source read-back is not written, but the fork path uses a filePath ThreadRef for the target, which is another sign that lifecycle thread identity is not consistently registry-id based.
epicCoverageAssessment: Flow 1 is incomplete against the written architecture and AC-1.7: launch resolution exists, but reload identity and resume selection still require human ruling or design update.
Flow 2 is covered by source and tests: ordered message mapping, turn derivation, runtime notes, idempotency, gaps, parallel tools, errors, and aborts are implemented.
Flow 3 is implemented with replay seeding and derived-form requeue; source immutability is covered.
Flow 4 is implemented through createModelCall over PI modelRegistry plus pi-ai dynamic import, with classified failures and closed-loop persisted outcomes covered.
Flow 5 is implemented: assignments load defaults/overrides, startup validation reports unreachable lanes, and capture continues.
Flow 6 is not fully covered: replay is deterministic and compares real read-back, but it consumes synthetic fixtures instead of recorded PI corpora required by AC-6.1.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapter was found in src capture/fork/inspect paths: capture uses real LHC intakeStream, fork replay uses intakeStream.messageEvents, and inspect reads real LHC surfaces.
Test-only model fakes are confined to test/fixtures and are not production code.
createModelCall does not fabricate output when pi-ai is missing; it returns a classified failure.

Material non-real verification path: packages/pi-lhc/test/fixtures/corpus.ts explicitly says loaders build synthetic stand-ins until M0 delivers recordings, so Flow 6 is not proving recorded PI corpus replay.

Material architecture drift: production index.ts persists threadRef in PI custom entries, despite tech-design.md stating the mapping persistence problem is dissolved and no session-file pointer is written.
Material resume limitation: production defaultSelectThread has no interactive operator selection path for multiple cwd-scoped threads.

blockingFindings.title: Capture verification uses synthetic stand-ins instead of recorded PI corpora
blockingFindings.evidence: epic.md:69 and epic.md:229-231 require recorded corpora replay through the converter. packages/pi-lhc/test/fixtures/corpus.ts:1-5 states the loaders build synthetic stand-ins until M0 delivers real recordings; loadAllCorpora at lines 137-149 returns only those synthetic loaders.

blockingFindings.title: Production --resume does not resolve an operator selection
blockingFindings.evidence: AC-1.7 in epic.md:141 requires --resume to resolve the operator's selection. index.ts:210-226 only notifies the candidate list and returns the single candidate or null for multiple candidates; thread-resolution.test.ts:255-292 asserts fail-closed behavior for multiple candidates rather than a selected thread.

blockingFindings.title: Reload identity reintroduced a PI custom-entry mapping contrary to the tech design
blockingFindings.evidence: tech-design.md:22 says there is no PI-session-to-thread mapping to persist, and tech-design.md:26 says appendEntry is moot for mapping because no session-file pointer is written. index.ts:134-158 defines pi-lhc-thread-state, index.ts:304-306 reads it from ctx.sessionManager.getEntries(), index.ts:468-469 appends the current threadRef, and index.ts:677-679 wires that append through pi.appendEntry.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Configured gates pass
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Ran pnpm --filter pi-lhc verify and pnpm --filter pi-lhc verify-all; both completed successfully with 20 test files and 143 tests passing.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Local PI and pi-ai type declarations are temporary boundaries
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: packages/pi-lhc/src/pi/types.ts declares the consumed PI API slice because the real package is not a workspace dependency; packages/pi-lhc/src/inference/pi-ai.ts provides local pi-ai typing while model-call dynamically imports @earendil-works/pi-ai at runtime.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Derived-form reuse remains deferred but correctness is preserved
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: fork.ts seeds forked threads by replay and does not copy ready derived forms; AC-3.3 permits requeue when reuse safety cannot be proven.

unresolvedItems: Add real recorded PI corpora or formally narrow AC-6.1 before passing the epic.
Human ruling or tech-design update needed for the PI custom-entry threadRef mapping introduced in index.ts.
Human ruling or PI API change needed for --resume operator selection in production.
If the custom-entry mapping is accepted, update the architecture docs and lifecycle tests so thread identity is consistently specified as registry threadId, including fork reload.
